title: Type Inference
instructions: When you call `listOf(1, 2, 3)`, how does Kotlin know it creates a `List<Int>`?

options.text: You must always write listOf<Int>(1, 2, 3) or it will not compile
Kotlin defaults to Int for all numbers
Type inference -- Kotlin figures out the type from the values you provide
listOf only works with Int values

explanation: Kotlin uses type inference to figure out that the values `1`, `2`, and `3` are all `Int` values. From this, it determines that `T` must be `Int`, so the result is `List<Int>`. You do not need to write the type explicitly. Type inference works with any type -- if you wrote `listOf("a", "b")`, Kotlin would infer `List<String>`.
